text:
Sampled HR@10 and full-catalog HR@10 measure different ranking problems; model ordering need not agree. RecSys 2025’s [sampling-reliability study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) separates model separability, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and alignment with fully observed preferences. [Rank-estimation research (2024)](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) likewise identifies sampling-induced rank bias. Practical implication: keep host validation unchanged; use fixed, unique candidate pools and chunked full-catalog scoring as complementary diagnostics. A single random-negative margin cannot establish top-10 retrieval quality.

Geometry and popularity warrant separate measurements. [Spectral analysis (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12008) links popularity amplification to the dominant score-matrix spectrum and dimensional collapse. [ACE (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29322) studies anisotropy specifically in LLM-derived sequential embeddings; its findings do not establish the same failure in ID-based GRU4Rec. Proposed panel: replay-target rank, uniform versus popularity-matched versus model-hard candidate difficulty, item-frequency strata, score/embedding norms, cosine similarity, and effective rank. Treat correlations as hypotheses rather than causal explanations; replaying training targets measures fit, not generalization.

For falsification, [sequence-shuffling research (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) tests whether sequential benchmarks actually reward order information. Proposed additional controls: shuffled histories and permuted user–target pairing, evaluated only in the diagnostic panel. [Distributionally informed evaluation (2024)](https://841.io/doc/disteval.html) motivates examining user-level variation and uncertainty. Use paired user bootstrap within each category, then recompute the four-category macro-average; retain all replay observations belonging to each sampled user. Predefine diagnostic directions and assess whether changes track host validation HR@10 across separate single-model conditions. Bootstrap intervals quantify user-sampling uncertainty, not training-seed uncertainty or repeated-search selection bias.
